title: Azerbaijani TTS (9.36M, 24 kHz, offline)
subtitle: Offline Azerbaijani text-to-speech, 2-4x real time on CPU
description:
A fully offline text-to-speech model that speaks Azerbaijani. 9.36M parameters, 24 kHz mono, 2-4x faster than real time on an ordinary laptop CPU, and it needs no internet at runtime - which makes it usable inside a Kaggle notebook with networking switched off.

This is the Azerbaijani voice of Avaz, an open-source text-to-speech project that runs on the device itself and aims at natural intonation on phones.

It started as a fine-tune of owensong/Inflect-Micro-v2 (Apache-2.0). This is the second Azerbaijani checkpoint, v2.1: it continues from the first on 23,088 clips distilled from a teacher TTS, reads stress from a stress frontend on top of eSpeak NG, and has a polished decoder. On 471 held-out sentences its Whisper word error is about 2.65% at variation 0.333 (the default is 0.3), against 4.84% for the first checkpoint and 2.07% for the teacher's recordings.

Try it in the browser, nothing installed: https://huggingface.co/spaces/ilqarrrr/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan

Code, tests and the full training pipeline: https://github.com/HuseynliIlqar/Inflect_Micro_v2_Azerbaijan

Limitations: one voice, no emotion control, no voice cloning. At 9.36M parameters the speech is clear but not fully natural. Yes/no questions end with falling pitch; m->n, b->d and q->k confusions remain at the edges of a sentence; harmonic clarity at 2-4 kHz is below the teacher's; intonation flattens over long sentences. The training audio is synthetic, distilled from a teacher TTS, so the quality ceiling is the teacher.

Training data: the first checkpoint, which v2.1 starts from, was trained on ughurabbasov/azerbaijani-tts-dataset. The dataset declares no licence file; its author confirmed in the HuggingFace community tab that anyone may use it, with attribution requested.

Runtime note: phonemisation goes through phonemizer and eSpeak NG, both GPL-3.0-or-later. Running is unaffected; redistributing a combined work brings those terms with it. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md in the repository.

Do not use this voice to impersonate a real person or to produce deceptive content.
provenanceSources: owensong/Inflect-Micro-v2 (Apache-2.0); ughurabbasov/azerbaijani-tts-dataset, used for the first checkpoint (no declared licence, author permits use with attribution); v2.1 continued on audio distilled from a teacher TTS
